title: Mitigating Redundancy in Deep Recommender Systems: A Field Importance Distribution Perspective

problem.claim: Redundant feature-field information in deep recommender systems increases computational cost and can reduce prediction performance.

gap.claim: Existing feature selection and embedding-size assignment methods do not jointly and effectively optimize feature fields because they are unstable, overlook inter-field importance relationships, and target different objectives.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes a distribution-based field optimization framework using importance distributions to address feature selection and embedding-size assignment together.
The framework trains a learner for each feature field to obtain stable and comprehensive importance information.
The framework removes noise features and assigns adaptive embedding sizes according to similarity in feature-field importance.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extremely low pre-training overhead, substantially reduced training and inference time, and more accurate prediction with fewer feature fields.

narrative_sequence.summary: CTR prediction requires learning user-item interaction features in recommender systems.
Redundancy creates computational cost and suboptimal performance, while existing removal strategies have complementary limitations.
The paper introduces importance-distribution-based field optimization with per-field learners, noise-feature elimination, and adaptive embedding sizes.
The authors report lower overhead and runtime, fewer feature fields, and improved prediction accuracy.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, baselines, quantitative results, or evaluation protocols.
The abstract does not describe the importance-distribution construction or learner architecture.
